lots.title: 2021 RDT 11B MINI EXCAVATOR WI...
lots.findings: NOT a book lot: the 'books' in the catalogue text are the machine's manuals, so the books-and-paper flag is a false match and there are no book titles, spines or title pages to read. The lot is a 1 tonne class Chinese mini excavator with attachments. Compliance plate (photo 6) reads: EXCAVATOR CE, Model RDT-11B, Engine YANMAR, Bucket capacity 0.02 m3, Operating weight 990KGS, Rated power 10KW, Date 01/2021, Serial No 210003. The rear hood decal reads 'POWERED BY YANMAR'. The boom decals read 'S.W.L. 90KG' and a model-style decal that looks like 'QM 12-3' (unclear). It has a canopy ROPS with an amber beacon, rubber tracks, a front blade, a fire extinguisher by the controls and a 'Hire' style sticker on the cab side. Attachments on two pallets (photos 10-11): hydraulic auger drive with hoses, two auger bits (about 12in and 6in, matching the catalogue), a rake, a ripper tine, a mud or batter bucket, a small trenching bucket, a larger digging bucket and quick hitch brackets. The catalogue claims of 2021 and the attachments are supported by the photos. The 40.7 hours is not visible in any photo (no hour meter shown).
lots.condition: Appears in good used order. Paint is mostly intact with light scuffing on the boom, bucket and blade. The canopy roof shows some sun fading. Attachments show normal use, surface rust and dirt. Running condition, hours and hydraulic leaks cannot be confirmed from the photos.
lots.identification: 2021 RDT-11B 1 tonne class Chinese mini excavator, Yanmar-powered (plate: 990 kg operating weight, 10 kW, serial 210003, 01/2021, CE), canopy ROPS, rubber tracks, front blade, with hydraulic auger drive, 2 augers, rake, ripper tine and 3 buckets. Not a book lot: the 'books' are machine manuals. Hours (40.7) not visible in photos.

lots.title: 1950'S JEEP PEDAL CAR
lots.findings: Pressed steel US Army style jeep pedal car, olive green, cartoon helmeted soldier (GI) decal and 'US' with star on both sides, 'M / NC 554' stencil on side, bonnet number partly legible (ending '7 A'), fold-down windscreen frame, chrome-capped pressed wheels with rubber tyres, red rear reflector, steering wheel, tow handle at rear. No maker plate read; style matches 1950s Murray or Australian Cyclops/Hamilton jeep pedal cars but maker not confirmed.
lots.condition: Original unrestored paint with heavy surface rust and wear, dents, rusted bumper, pedal crank present; appears complete.
lots.identification: Cyclops (Cyclops & Lines Bros, Australia) Army Jeep pedal car, pressed steel Willys-style jeep, c1955-1965. Olive green, original unrestored paint with heavy surface rust. Bonnet stencil reads '1351507-A' (faint; matches the hood number on reproduction Cyclops Army Jeep decal sets sold on eBay AU), white stars on the body, 'US' with a cartoon helmeted GI head decal and 'M / NC 554' on both sides. Fold-down windscreen frame (no glass/perspex, typical), slotted grille with two headlight bosses, front bumper, rear grab handle, red rear reflector, white pressed-steel wheels with chrome hubcaps and rubber tyres, white steering wheel. Pedal crank and pedals appear present. Lines Bros (Tri-ang) owned Cyclops from 1955, and the body is the Australian cousin of the Tri-ang Willys jeep pedal car. Lot estimate A$350-500.

lots.title: EARLY 1900'S ENAMEL ADVERTISIN...
lots.findings: Blue and white enamel advertising strip sign 'THE LEADER PRICE 3D'. The Leader was a Melbourne weekly (catalogue says Tasmanian origin, unverified). No maker name visible on front.
lots.condition: Chipping and rust loss around all edges and mounting holes, some to lower letters; face mostly intact and bright.
lots.identification: Vitreous enamel strip advertising sign, white letters on dark blue: 'THE LEADER  PRICE 3d.' About 15 x 54 cm, flat steel, fixing holes at corners. Newspaper vendor's sign, almost certainly for The Leader, the Melbourne weekly (1862-1957, sister paper of The Age); catalogue's 'Tasmanian origin' is unverified (there was a Hobart paper called The Leader in the 1860s, but at a penny, and too early for an enamel sign). Genuine age wear: heavy rust/chip loss along the top edge, both corners and bottom edge, a big chip under the 'A', face otherwise bright and glossy. Looks period (c1900-1930), not a reproduction.

lots.title: VINTAGE CAST IRON FIRE ALARM C...
lots.findings: Cast iron arched fire alarm call box: 'BREAK THE GLASS PRESS THE BUTTON' around the glass window, script monogram cast below (possibly 'NSWG' or similar, uncertain), 'FIRE ALARM', 'FIRE' painted on the side. Interior retains the code wheel transmitter mechanism (toothed alarm code wheel with clockwork), relay coils, terminal block and a bakelite style telephone handset in the cabinet.
lots.condition: Red paint heavily worn and flaking, rust inside and on door; glass missing or broken; mechanism dirty and corroded, working order unknown.
lots.identification: Australian fire brigade cast iron fire alarm box (street/building call box), arched-top door, red paint. Door cast 'BREAK THE GLASS PRESS THE BUTTON' around a round window (glass gone, button plate rusty), a script monogram below, then 'FIRE ALARM'; 'FIRE' painted on the side. Inside: complete alarm transmitter with toothed code wheel (painted dial), clockwork, relay coils, terminal block, bell, and a bakelite telephone handset on a hook, i.e. the 'fire alarm telephone' type used by Australian brigades (probably c1930s-1950s). Monogram is very worn: most likely 'NSWFB' (New South Wales Fire Brigades) in the same script style as the NSWFB box sold on eBay, but could be MFB; not certain. About 40-45 cm high judging by photos (not given).
